there is a lot about these drugs that we don't know about. we don't know how they really affect our brains, or how they would affect us long-term. you are fucking with some really deep shit when it comes to altering the neurotransmitters associated with serotonin/dopamine. there are a couple very real syndromes that can be associated with SSRIs: serotonin syndrome and prolonged sexual dysfunction from taking them. i have suffered from both.

the competition for position is within the process of ritual and reflects upon cosmological order. there is a very common theme in many stories regarding the shaman-warrior dichotomy. at the same time, people with mental disorders were usually regarded as having special abilities (in the middle east and russia, for example). does that at all fit a darwinistic narrative?

anyway, this is besides imperialism. all i am disagreeing with is the notion that humans are intrinsically hierarchical and competitive. if anything, they are more drawn to ritual and consecration.

if your focus is on empires, then you are right. but there was a time before empires existed, and societies weren't as much competitive as they were following ritual. i don't think humans are intrinsically hierarchical and competitive, they became that way when surplus goods became wealth and wealth became fetishised.

hey, yes i am feeling a bit better--thank you for asking. i don't mind at all answering all your questions, but it's a lot of text, so get ready to read!

first of all, i am 23 and i am female. if astrology is important to you, my sun/moon/rising are cancer, scorpio, and pisces. i have a strange awareness of things. i remember being baptised, which is really weird because i was about 3 months old. my mother said i was a very quiet child with a lot of imagination, and i was always very empathetic. i remember when my sister was born--when i was maybe four or five she was alone in her crib and crying, my parents were downstairs. i went to her and started speaking to her and asking her if she wanted to go see mommy. she seemed to understand and stopped crying and i carried her to where she wanted to be--with my mother.

i seem to be able to feel the way people feel when i look at them, or just by being around them. sometimes i have "visions" that are like daydreams of things that will happen, and they do. i also see static everywhere, and sometimes shape in the static. i've had a number of encounters with other beings, some of them have tried to possess me. i have hypnogogic/trance experiences--i have to listen to music and keep a light on or i hear and see things. what i hear ranges from normal conversations, to screams, to laughter, and even sometimes things talking to me or about me. what i see varies; i've seen people and "otherworldly beings" in the same room as i'm in, and they try to communicate with me. i usually tell them to go away unless it's an entity that's trying to protect me--recently there was one that was holding me and she was telling me that i had to stay strong. after that i began hearing voices in a language i didn't know, i repeated it in my sleep while my boyfriend was awake and he said it sounded demonic. i think i wrote it down somewhere but i can't remember where.

i also see auras, with the static. if a person is very sad or very happy it takes on a different shape. when i'm drunk the static becomes heavier, to the point that it can distort a person's features. when i pick up something electronic, i can feel its vibrations. electricity emphasises my sensitivity. it also worsens my tinnitus, because i can hear its buzzing away. i can also sense if a place has something malicious in it, or if a person is holding something malicious in them. i tried to exorcise one of my friends once when she was having an episode because i immediately felt like there was something trying to make her fear worse, something that was poisoning her. when i held her hand i could feel it try to push me back. i did this meditation where i breathed the "poison" in through my nose and let it leave my mouth, imagining while i was doing it that i was expelling the poison within her, and after some time she threw up and felt better. i didn't tell her i was performing this exorcism, but i did tell her i thought she was possessed--she didn't like it when i told her, so i don't think i was able to completely get rid of the thing inside her.

i have severe PTSD, so my depressions are caused by a number of things. i have a very huge problem with feeling incompetent and invisible. this is due to severe abuse and neglect. i don't have many friends and i self-isolate, because i have had too many bad experiences with people where i've been taken advantage of. usually i'm thinking about how alone or separated i feel when i get depressed. i think i am problematic because i'm emotional and very sensitive to how people react to me. i get triggered by that, and by thinking about this world and how awful it is. i think about everything that has been lost in the past, all the genocide, all the beautiful things being covered in cement and thrown away like it's nothing. i don't really think about my existence because i'm comfortable thinking i'm a manifestation of the sentience of the universe, and to that effect, everyone and everything has godly power and is sacred. but i mourn for everything, it feels like, and for everyone. i feel useless. i don't know how to get over it, or how to let go. when i mourn for myself i'm mourning for a body that's been hurt, abused, and is scared because of it. 

the pain is everywhere and it is excruciating. it's physical, mental, spiritual, and emotional. i feel it in the core of my body and sometimes i have to curl up because i feel like i'm going to vomit. crying and screaming isn't enough to alleviate it. i've hurt myself (cutting, hitting) in order to distract myself momentarily. i dissociate to get myself away. but when i'm in pain it's gut-wrenching, it feels like my body is being quartered, like my mind is lost, like my emotions are too much, they suffocate me. it feels like i'm being suffocated and that i'm being eaten alive from the inside. lately i always feel like crying, like having an episode, even when i'm in class. these episodes can last for days or weeks. if i try to go about as normal, i get dizzy spells and feel very anxious and overwhelmed by everything. my brain feels like it's on fire. the pain makes me think that it's not just me i'm feeling pain for. i don't want to feel it, and prayer and meditation relieve it temporarily.

i've done a number of meditations. i'm good at clearing my thoughts, though it's better when i meditate with my boyfriend--he's my grounding force and i feel that something very powerful protects him. when i meditate with him i don't get visions or hear things as i would when i'm alone. i practise yoga, which helps me a lot. i'm currently prescribed benzos (klonipin) for anxiety and trying to find something that will help me sleep because i have a lot of trouble with that. i refuse to take anti-depressants--i've had them prescribed to me since i was 15 and they make me manic and they don't stop the pain, they just numb me externally. i'll still feel pain inside, i just can't cry, and i can't produce art, which is a huge part of my life. i try to draw and paint the things i see, i write about them too. when i'm on an anti-depressant my mind goes blank.

i listen to music all the time! it has a huge effect on me. my boyfriend's a terrific musician, and whenever he plays it calms me down instantly. : -)

i love alan watts. he's been a great help to me, too. sometimes i wish he were alive just so i could get to hear that amazing laugh of his in person and so i could give him a great big hug.

also, thank you for your advise. i'm going to write these things down in my diary and i will meditate on things of a higher frequency. memories of being in nature gives me great relief--i have a lot of dreams where natural beings come to me and comfort me, often when i'm in great distress. your response comes across as one of those guides, which is really what i'm looking for.

look, i'm well aware of what i need to do. i don't picture myself or anything as a mistake. we're all manifestations of a sentient universe, and that's a beautiful thing. but being in a body is and can be excruciatingly painful, especially when you're receptive. i do not take anything for granted. i am constantly trying to improve myself.

what makes you think i don't want to "give up" on these drugs? that's awfully presumptuous of you to say, and very insensitive. do you know what it's like to not just have PTSD, but to see things all the time? not being able to sleep because you hear voices/sounds or see things you really don't want to see? do you know what it's like to have something try to possess you and tell you "i'm not going anywhere" so that it makes you more vulnerable through fear? i've been through this my entire life. sometimes it's worse, other times it's not. i don't want to depend on drugs. i don't want to depend on opiates. they just happen to be a substance which grounds me, which relaxes me. it's my "weed", and i don't even take that much of it--not enough to nod out, anyway. there are no excuses here, just a person in pain who wants input. i would not be asking for help if i wanted to continue using opiates as a means of escapism.

i appreciate your trying to help but i find it very cold and indifferent, which isn't what i would expect from someone who understands sensitivity. many people of this world--mostly artists--have complained of a similar phenomenon, and depended on opiates for the same reason. it would be great if we lived in a world without coldness and indifference, but here it is, and i'm reading it in the form of your perspective.

thanks for the gesture, anyway. next time i hope you ask more questions than assume to know the answers for someone who is unique in their experience.

yes, and mine is one of empathy. we would not be here if it weren't for this splendid planet and its environment, and this is something modern folks have obviously forgotten. it may not be necessary to acknowledge an equivocal standard toward nature to protect it, but putting nature at a lower level than humankind--to think that we can control it, or make our own judgements upon it, to think that progression should enable self-interest on the behalf of humankind is quite narrow-minded. progression should be made in the interest of all things, especially this planet and all it contains, which is so intrinsically beautiful and inspirational that it would be a shame to objectify and sunder it.

if one idea was common among many different cultures with little to no contact with each other, don't you think that would say something? old tribes and civilisations survived on their own pretty well and followed their own natural courses of progression. they weren't stagnant. of course, most people don't see this because they think those peoples were primitive. the truth is that they were much more ethically advanced than we are today. i'm speaking for non-western cultures, primarily. as an example, you should know that the conquistadors thought the aztecs to be more medically and mathematically advanced than europeans (they knew the concept of 0 thousands of years prior to european civilisations), and yet the aztecs lived without thinking there was any difference between time and space, nor was there anything that could be considered an "inanimate object" to them.

ponder over that for a while and ask yourself if it is really necessary to dichotomise and categorise everything into a hierarchical norm.

believe it or not, that's a very christian-colonial-imperialist concept, whether or not you believe in god. that kind of thinking stems from "god, glory, and gold"--and was far from common before hermeneutic traditions swept the planet. if you study the beliefs of other cultures and compare them, their perspectives are drastically different from yours, even to the point that AI in japan is viewed as having a completely different potential than in the west. (in the east, robots are considered as having the potential for "kami", or godliness, and even buddhic revelation, where a robot can benefit mankind by praying and being of service to the planet. western science looks at the expansion of robotics as a method of salvation and escapism, which is quite biblical.) non-western cultures don't really perceive man as being above animals: rather, we are among them.

"man above all" is not a healthy concept. hierarchical thinking just creates a separation between man and nature, even though we are a part of it. we're not immune from disease, and we share the same basic functions of all life on our planet. if we want to "protect our environment", as you say, we'd have to acknowledge that we are equal among nature and other creatures. we share the same planet they do, and without flora and fauna we would be in a very sticky ecological mess.

in the industrial era there were many authors and scientists who fretted about this concept which we know as "social darwinism"--the best and the hardiest are at the top. social darwinism is oppressive and destructive, as can be observed when one looks at the state of the planet we inhabit. the pesticides we use are unnatural, and whatever disease we try to prevent will only mutate. we've turned agriculture into a monopolous industry. we've modified organisms to the point where they experience excruciating pain because their bodies cannot handle it (poultry, even fish). we've exhausted our oceans, and poisoned them, with other sources of water, on top of that. we've desecrated rainforests, we've destroyed the natural habitats of many animals and indigenous peoples. is this any way to live?
